questions.stem: Explain the following culinary terms: (a) au gratin (b) mise en place (c) blanch (d) sauté. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Au gratin: sprinkled with cheese or breadcrumbs and browned under a grill or in an oven
2 marks: Mise en place: preparing and arranging everything needed before service or cooking
2 marks: Blanch: plunging food briefly into boiling water then into cold water, or bringing to the boil, to whiten, loosen skins or set colour
2 marks: Sauté: tossing or cooking quickly in a little hot fat
questions.explanation: Au gratin means browned with cheese or crumbs; mise en place is advance preparation; blanching briefly boils then cools food; sautéing cooks quickly in little fat with tossing.

questions.stem:
(a) What is cross-contamination? [2 marks]
(b) State three ways of preventing cross-contamination in a catering kitchen. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Transfer of harmful bacteria from raw food, surfaces or people to ready-to-eat food
2 marks: Use colour-coded chopping boards and knives for raw and cooked foods
2 marks: Store raw meat below cooked food in the refrigerator, covered
2 marks: Wash hands and sanitise surfaces between tasks
questions.explanation: Cross-contamination moves bacteria from raw to ready-to-eat food. Prevent it with colour-coded equipment, correct storage and handwashing and sanitising.

questions.topic: Principles of cooking methods and practical demonstrations
questions.stem:
(a) Describe braising as a method of cooking. [4 marks]
(b) State two advantages of braising and two foods suitable for it. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Food is browned, then partly covered with liquid or sauce
2 marks: Cooked slowly in a covered pan, usually in the oven
1 mark: Advantage: tenderises tougher, cheaper cuts
1 mark: Advantage: retains flavour and nutrients in the sauce
1 mark: Food: stewing beef or oxtail
1 mark: Food: whole fish, chicken pieces or vegetables such as cabbage
questions.explanation: Braising browns food then cooks it slowly in a covered pan with some liquid, tenderising tough cuts and keeping flavour. Suitable for stewing beef, oxtail, chicken and cabbage.

questions.topic: Types of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks, giving two examples of each. [4 marks]
(b) Name four non-alcoholic drinks served in restaurants. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Fermented drinks: produced by yeast acting on sugars
1 mark: Examples: wine, beer, palm wine (any two)
1 mark: Distilled drinks (spirits): fermented liquor heated and the alcohol vapour condensed
1 mark: Examples: gin, whisky, rum, brandy (any two)
1 mark: Mineral or table water
1 mark: Fruit juices
1 mark: Malt drinks or soft drinks
1 mark: Tea, coffee or zobo
questions.explanation: Fermented drinks such as wine and beer come from yeast fermentation; spirits such as gin and rum are distilled. Non-alcoholic drinks include water, juices, malt, soft drinks, tea, coffee and zobo.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a cyclical menu and a function (banquet) menu. [4 marks]
(b) State four points to consider when planning a menu for a school dining hall. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Cyclical menu: set of menus repeated in rotation over a fixed period, used in institutions
2 marks: Function menu: pre-arranged menu for a special event, fixed number of guests and price
1 mark: Nutritional needs of growing students
1 mark: Budget/cost per head
1 mark: Variety, cultural and religious requirements
1 mark: Equipment, staff and time available
questions.explanation: Cyclical menus rotate in institutions; function menus are agreed for events. School menus must meet nutrition, budget, variety and cultural needs within available resources.
